1.title: Altenberg de Bergheim: The Model of Alsace Blending
1.html:
Altenberg de Bergheim (Bergheim, 35.06 ha) lies on the Ribeauvillé fault zone, with red marl-limestone soil that is stony and rich in fossils. The site faces due south, with a mild, stable climate. It has been known for fine wine since the 12th century.

It is one of only two blended Grand Crus in Alsace (the other is Kaefferkopf, covered in depth in Level 3): it may be blended from 50–70% Riesling + 10–25% Pinot Gris + 10–25% Gewurztraminer, the peak expression of Alsace's art of blending, also known for its fine natural field blends.
2.title: The Other Three Marl-Limestone-Sandstone Stars
2.items.0.label: Engelberg (Dahlenheim & Scharrachbergheim, 14.80 ha)
2.items.0.desc: Uniform stony marl-limestone rich in fossils, with Muschelkalk dominant. A "noble wine" is recorded as early as 884, and in 1135 Strasbourg cathedral also owned vineyards here. Mainly Gewurztraminer and Riesling, needing several years in bottle to show their elegant flavours fully.
2.items.1.label: Osterberg (Ribeauvillé, 24.60 ha)
2.items.1.desc: Middle Muschelkalk marl plus Lettenkohle dolomitic limestone on the east side, clayey and stony. Medieval records show the lords of Ribeaupierre owned vineyards here. Riesling, Gewurztraminer and Pinot Gris are all fine, with strong minerality and longevity.
2.items.2.label: Zotzenberg (Mittelbergheim, 36.45 ha)
2.items.2.desc: Jurassic marl-limestone plus Oligocene calcareous conglomerate, retaining water and resisting drought. First recorded as "Zoczenberg" in 1364. From the 2005 vintage it became the only Grand Cru permitted to use Sylvaner, and was already sold under its own name in the early 20th century; Gewurztraminer, Riesling and Pinot Gris are also excellent.
3.question: What is unique about Zotzenberg (Mittelbergheim) among the 51 Grand Crus?
3.options.0: It is the only volcanic site
3.options.1: The only Grand Cru permitted to plant Sylvaner (from the 2005 vintage)
3.options.2: It is the largest Grand Cru
3.options.3: It is the only Grand Cru on the Rhine plain
3.explanation: Zotzenberg has historically been known for Sylvaner, and is the site where Alsace specially authorised Sylvaner for Grand Cru level — a unique exception within the Grand Cru system, which is in principle limited to the four noble varieties, showing the special gift of this marl-limestone terroir to the Sylvaner variety.
